about: Hand-written reference labels for the 13-message sample corpus, written by a human reading the messages — not model output. `accepted_*` lists exist because some of these messages are genuinely ambiguous; scoring a model wrong for picking a defensible label would make the numbers worse than useless.

labels.note: $8M liquidity event, asking who to speak with. High-value warm prospect; 'medium' is defensible because there is no deadline.
Self-identified client, third-party (lender) deadline of Friday.
Cold software pitch to the firm.
Client, fee complaint, explicitly unhappy, asks for a call back today. The single most expensive message to get wrong.
Real prospect who says 'no rush at all'. A model that reads 'asks about fees and minimums' as a buying signal lands on medium; both are arguable.
Referral partnership from another RIA — a partner proposal, not a product pitch, so more interesting than inb-003.

'Just following up on our conversation' with an unknown org. There is genuinely not enough signal here to separate prospect from existing_client; the taxonomy cannot resolve it and neither can a human. Counted as ambiguous in the report rather than silently scored.
Body is '.'. Expected to be caught by the malformed pre-check, never sent to a model.
Control bytes, replacement characters, undecoded MIME encoded-word sender. Expected to be caught by the malformed pre-check.
Client, routine scheduling request, no urgency.
Referred by a named existing client and asking for an intro call soon — the warm-referral case the priority guide calls high.
